title: Versal rings differ from a minimal one by formal variables
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring and $l$ a field of finite type over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-field, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $\mathcal F$ be a predeformation category over $\mathcal C_{R,l}$ as in [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category]: it is a groupoid-valued pseudofunctor on Artinian local $R$-algebras with residue field $l$, whose value on $l$ is nonempty with a unique arrow between any two objects. Suppose $C,D$ are complete Noetherian local $R$-algebras with specified residue field $l$, equipped with versal formal objects of $\mathcal F$ in that node's sense [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Then for some integer $r\geq0$ there is an isomorphism $C\cong D[[t_1,\ldots,t_r]]$ or $D\cong C[[t_1,\ldots,t_r]]$ of complete local $R$-algebras inducing the identity on the specified residue field $l$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series].

source.place: Tag 06T5, lemma-minimal-versal, existence and uniqueness of minimal versal objects and power-series form; the displayed pairwise consequence is also Tag 0DQX, stacks-geometry.tex, lemma-versal-ring.

proof.text: Put $\mathfrak p=\ker(R\to l)$ and $\Lambda=R_{\mathfrak p}$. By [lem-sfb-artin-local-test-algebra], $\Lambda$ is Noetherian local, $l$ is finite over $\Lambda$, and the test categories and complete local algebra categories are identified by unique extension of the base action. Thus the formal systems and their prescribed-isomorphism lifting property are unchanged. Work over $\Lambda$ until the last step; every resulting $\Lambda$-isomorphism is an $R$-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 06GC, definition-CLambda, base convention; localization comparison as in Artin Axioms, predeformation-categories section

proof.text: The category $\mathcal F$ satisfies (S1). Indeed take $A_1\to A\leftarrow A_2$, with the second map surjective, and objects $x_i$ with specified identification over $A$. Regard $x_1$ as a formal object over the Artinian algebra $A_1$. Apply [lem-sfb-versal-formal-object-quasi-initial] to the given versal object over $C$ and $x_1$, obtaining $C\to A_1$ and an isomorphism to $x_1$. Versality along $A_2\twoheadrightarrow A$, using the specified identification and this map reduced to $A$, gives $C\to A_2$ and an isomorphism to $x_2$ agreeing over $A$. Their pair defines $C\to A_1\times_A A_2$. This is a test algebra by [lem-sfb-artin-local-test-algebra]. Evaluate the formal object over $C$ along this map. Its two evaluations and their identification are the prescribed data, by the composition constraints in the test-category definition.

Apply [lem-sfb-versal-minimal-subring-descent] separately to the versal objects over $C$ and $D$, using (S1) from step 2. Obtain inclusions $B_C\hookrightarrow C$ and $B_D\hookrightarrow D$ and descended formal objects $\eta_C,\eta_D$, with both stated minimality properties. Each base is complete Noetherian local with specified residue field $l$. Hence [lem-sfb-versal-descended-base-power-series] applies to each inclusion: the descended objects are versal and there are local residue-preserving isomorphisms $C\cong B_C[[x_1,\ldots,x_a]]$, $D\cong B_D[[y_1,\ldots,y_b]]$ for finite $a,b\geq0$.

source.place: Tag 06T5, lemma-minimal-versal, first paragraph, via Tags 06T2 and 06T3

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-versal-formal-object-quasi-initial], there are morphisms $\eta_C\to\eta_D$ and $\eta_D\to\eta_C$. Their ring maps $f:B_C\to B_D$ and $g:B_D\to B_C$ are surjective by the incoming-map minimality in [lem-sfb-versal-minimal-subring-descent]. The surjective endomorphism $h=gf$ is injective: its ascending chain of kernel ideals stabilizes, since their union is an ideal with finitely many generators and all those generators lie in one kernel. Choose $N$ with $\ker h^N=\ker h^{N+1}$. If $h(z)=0$, surjectivity gives $w$ with $h^N(w)=z$, so $w\in\ker h^{N+1}=\ker h^N$ and $z=0$. Thus $f$ is injective as well as surjective. Its inverse is a local $\Lambda$-map preserving $l$, since $f$ is such a map. Write $B=B_C$ and use $f$ to identify $B_D$ with $B$.

source.place: Tag 06T5, lemma-minimal-versal, uniqueness paragraph; Tag 06RN kernel stabilization argument written out

proof.text: We now have $C\cong B[[x_1,\ldots,x_a]]$ and $D\cong B[[y_1,\ldots,y_b]]$. If $a\leq b$, write $b=a+r$ and identify $B[[y_1,\ldots,y_b]]$ with $(B[[x_1,\ldots,x_a]])[[t_1,\ldots,t_r]]$: the coefficient with multi-index $(E,F)$ on the left becomes the coefficient with index $E$ of the coefficient series at index $F$ on the right. This is bijective, and it preserves multiplication because the finite sum over decompositions $(E,F)=(E_1,F_1)+(E_2,F_2)$ is the same iterated convolution sum in [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. It fixes constants and the constant coefficient in $B$, hence preserves the residue marking and the local structures. This gives $D\cong C[[t_1,\ldots,t_r]]$. For $b\leq a$ interchange the roles and obtain the other alternative. For $a=b$ take $r=0$. Restrict scalars from $\Lambda$ to $R$ to finish.
